cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The parcel depot closes at six. Your mother's waiting outside the station. Which am I collecting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then do you want her waiting for me or waiting for her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Shall I pull over to explain, or keep driving before the depot shuts?

mechanism: A authorizes only one collection priority and makes B choose again when communication itself competes with the deadline.
confusable: Simple efficient routing could do both; the Drive needs mutually pressing duties and the Stance must rule on B proposed resolution.
comparison: Depot closure and a waiting parent create travel urgency, distinct from the kitchen scene hands-on simultaneous chores.
seedUse: Use D34-b birthday parcel and incoming call, with S01 approval governing which task may delay the other.
